About this Report

As a non-financial report publicly disclosed by Beijing Enterprises Water Group Limited, this report aims at responding to the expectations of stakeholders and comprehensively demonstrating the Group's concepts, management, actions and achievements in environmental, social and governance ("ESG") and sustainable development. This report has been reviewed and approved by the Board of Directors (the "Board") of Beijing Enterprises Water Group Limited, which guarantees that there are no false records, misleading statements or material omissions in this report.

Reporting Period

The reporting period is from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025. Information beyond this scope will be specified in related sections.

Reporting Scope

All information and data disclosed are from Beijing Enterprises Water Group Limited and its subsidiaries. The data covers the Group's headquarters and its subsidiaries that hold operational control. Data from subsidiaries with common financial control but autonomous implementation of operational policies is not reported.

Abbreviations

For the convenience of expression and reading, this report refers to Beijing Enterprises Water Group Limited and its subsidiaries as "BEWG", "the Group" and "We".

Reporting Principles

This report is prepared in adherence to the principles of "Materiality", "Quantitative", "Balance" and "Consistency".

Materiality: The Board and the Sustainability Committee have identified, evaluated and reviewed significant ESG matters. This report published ESG matters based on the materiality assessment results.

Quantitative: This report referred to applicable quantification standards and practices, adopted a quantitative approach to measuring and disclosing applicable key performance indicators. The measurement criteria, methods, assumptions and/or calculation tools as well as the source of conversion factors used for the key performance indicators in this report, where applicable, are described accordingly.

Balance: This report provided the BEWG's 2025 sustainability performance and outputs through fair presentation without any misstatement, inappropriate content and omissions.

Consistency: The statistical calibre of the quantitative data has changed compared to previous years, and the changes have been explained in the corresponding positions in this report. The statistical and calculation methods for quantitative data are consistent with previous years.

Data Explanation

All data disclosed in this report are from the Group's internal collection and statistics, and reports from its subsidiaries. The currency unit in this report is RMB unless otherwise specified. Any discrepancy between the total number and the sum of the values listed or between the percentages and their calculations disclosed in the report is due to rounding.

Reporting Guidelines

This report is in accordance with the requirements of Appendix C2 Environmental, Social and Governance Reporting Code (ESG Reporting Code) of the Rules Governing the Listing of Securities on the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Limited (the "Listing Rules"), with reference to the GRI Sustainability Reporting Standards (GRI Standards) issued by the Global Sustainability Standard Board (GSSB), and other standards.

Confirmation and Approval

After confirmation by management, this report was reviewed and approved by the Board on 25 March 2026.

Access to this Report

This report is available in Chinese and English on the Group's website (https://www.bewg.net/en/). In case of any conflict or inconsistency between the Chinese and English versions, the Chinese version shall prevail; in case of any conflict or inconsistency between this report and the annual report of the Group, the annual report shall prevail.

Board Statement

BEWG has established an effective ESG governance system with clearly defined responsibilities, through which the Group deeply integrates ESG concepts into its operations and development to strengthen its core competitiveness.

Supervision on ESG matters

BEWG has established a management system covering the Board, the Sustainability Committee and the ESG Working Group. The Board, as the highest decision-making body on ESG matters, takes full responsibility for the ESG strategy and ESG disclosure of the Group. The Sustainability Committee is responsible for overseeing and reporting to the Board on the implementation and achievements of ESG management. The functions of each level of the management system are detailed in the "ESG Governance" section in Chapter 01.

ESG Management Guidelines and Strategies

BEWG maintains active communication with all stakeholders, keeps abreast of key ESG concerns in capital markets and the industry, regularly identifies and assesses material ESG issues, and continuously optimises its ESG governance and management mechanisms. The Board is involved in evaluating and prioritising key ESG issues. It regularly reviews the ESG strategy based on the materiality matrix, and analyses and assesses the potential impact of each material issue on the Group's ESG strategy. BEWG highly values the significance of ESG-related risks and opportunities and their potential major impacts, including those brought by climate change, and has incorporated them into the Group's overall risk management system. The Board oversees the assessment of ESG-related risks and opportunities, ensuring the Group has established sound and effective ESG risk management and internal control systems. This year, the Group continued to refine the internal process to identify, assess, and manage climate-related risks and opportunities. We carried out risk identification, assessment, and management for ESG issues, such as operational compliance, information security, and human resource management. For more information, please refer to the "Climate Change" section of this report and the "Corporate Governance Report - Risk Management and Internal Control" section in the annual report.

Review of ESG Targets

In line with its business characteristics, BEWG has set a series of ESG management targets regarding water saving, energy saving, emission reduction, quality and safety, etc. The Board regularly reviews the progress of ESG-related targets, oversees and evaluates their fulfillment throughout the reporting period to ensure the facilitation of ESG governance across the Group.

The ESG progress and achievements of BEWG in 2025 have been fully and truly disclosed in this report, which was reviewed by the Sustainability Committee and approved by the Board on 25 March 2026.

Message from the Chairman

Water governance follows constant principles, and so too does enterprise management. As we approach the culmination of "14th Five-Year Plan" period, BEWG has remained steadfast in its commitment to national priorities, navigating by the blueprint set forth at the National People's Congress and attuning ourselves to the evolving imperatives of the new development paradigm. Amid profound external changes, we have aligned our efforts with national strategies, embedding green transformation into the core of our growth. Through pragmatic action and innovative thinking, we have turned challenges into opportunities. With water as our medium, we contribute to painting a more sustainable future; with our enterprise as the vessel, we sail forward on the course of high-quality development. In doing so, we strive to deliver outcomes that meet the demands of the times and lives up to our mission and responsibility.

Those who advance with vision uphold sound governance as their cornerstone. At BEWG, we understand that excellence in business is built on robust governance. To this end, we continuously enhance our corporate governance structure and risk management mechanisms, embedding compliance, integrity, and transparency into every layer of our operations as the essential groundwork for sustainable progress. Guided by the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and our "W.I.S.E." action direction, we have integrated ESG deeply into our corporate strategy, advancing with conviction on a path of high-quality, sustainable development. This commitment has been reflected in our recognition as "China's Top 10 Most Influential Water Companies" for 15 consecutive years, and our inclusion in S&P Global's Sustainability Yearbook (China Edition) for the fourth year in a row. Looking forward, BEWG will keep learning and improving, transforming each milestone into renewed momentum to build a legacy that stands the test of time and contributes meaningfully to the world we share.

Clear waters carry profound responsibility, and green mountains reward those who protect them. At BEWG, we recognise that safeguarding our rivers and waterways is a solemn duty entrusted to us. Guided by the vision of "keeping the water of life evergreen", we embed green practices throughout the entire water cycle. We pursue excellence in securing safe water supply, advance wastewater reuse and resource recovery through relentless innovation, and transform every water plant into a green engine that powers vibrant communities. Confronting climate change, we actively pursue China's "dual carbon" goals by integrating energy conservation

and emissions reduction across our operations. Through smart management and technological innovation, we continue to reduce our environmental footprint. For us, responsible water management means embracing ecological stewardship. That is why we direct our expertise toward restoring rivers, lakes, and wetlands, protecting biodiversity, and living in harmony with nature, so that clear waters flow and green landscapes thrive for generations to come.

Like water that nourishes all things, true virtue lies in lasting contribution. At BEWG, we believe that a company's value extends beyond commercial success, it is also defined by its commitment to society and its role in enriching people's lives. In 2025, we fortified our operational resilience, anchoring long-term value in responsibility. Internally, we have built a culture of trust and inclusion, empowered our people with effective mechanisms, and placed safety at the core of their growth so that every member of BEWG can find belonging in trust and achieve their potential with dignity. Externally, we serve our clients with dedication, partner with integrity, and contribute to industry progress, ensuring that stakeholder confidence and satisfaction remain our unwavering pursuit. In 2025, we launched the "Smart Water Dual Engine" intelligent solution, driving the cloud-based upgrade of our operational management and smart control platforms, and expanding the large-scale application of AI across the water value chain. Our "Cloud-Chain-Unit" operational paradigm was comprehensively upgraded, gradually delivering scaled efficiencies through intensive management. Overseas, we advanced equipment exports and achieved breakthroughs in our asset-light business model.

Where determination leads, even mountains and oceans can be crossed. As we enter the "15th Five-Year Plan" period, BEWG remains firmly committed to keeping the basic business position with cash flow first, securing operational foundations while maintaining strategic focus, accelerating digital-intelligent integration, and advancing ecological stewardship. Guided by technological innovation to cultivate new productive forces, we will join hands with partners across sectors and move resolutely toward our vision of becoming a trusted and leading world-class water environmental services provider.

Message from the CEO

Looking back at 2025, the global situation became increasingly complex, and the climate pressure continued to intensify. The water utilities industry, as the cornerstone of ecological civilisation and sustainable development, has never been more important. Against the backdrop of industry transformation and higher expectations for sustainability, BEWG has always followed the "W.I.S.E." action direction, unwavering in our commitment to public welfare, deepening digital-intelligent operations, and delivering on our responsibility to protect ecosystems. Moving forward, we will remain focused on our core mission, strengthen operational excellence, and work alongside partners to secure water safety, improve efficiency, and restore aquatic ecosystems, thereby consolidating the foundation of water resilience essential to sustainable development under Chinese modernisation.

Water sustains life in the present and shapes development in the future. At BEWG, we are committed to ensuring water safety and fostering the sustainable use of this vital resource. We continuously advance key initiatives including water quality enhancement, leakage control, sewage treatment, and emergency response. Over the past year, we have safeguarded water supply quality through internal control systems that exceed national standards, reduced network leakage with intelligent monitoring and driven sewage treatment efficiency under our "Digital Star-level" operational framework. At the same time, we have actively expanded the reuse of reclaimed water, built regional water circulation networks, and extended water-saving awareness to public education, working with all sectors of society to safeguard water resources for the future.

Smart water drives efficiency while innovation opens new frontiers. At BEWG, we see digital-intelligent transformation as a strategic pivot for the future, reshaping water operations through our "cloud-chain-unit" paradigm and continuously advancing the standardisation, intelligence, and intensification of water plant management. With the help of the SED platform and our "Digital Star-level" evaluation system, we are moving operations from experience-based practice to intelligent decision-making. Through process AI and smart IoT, we enable precise control and efficiency improvement, while embedding business-finance integration and AI agents to redefine risk management and decision-making processes. Beyond this, we continue to strengthen innovation R&D and cybersecurity, leading the industry's future with "X Water", developing talent through industry-education partnerships, and collaborating across sectors to create a smarter, greener, and more sustainable water journey.

Clear water illuminates the way forward and benevolent water nourishes all. At BEWG, sound governance, integrity, and prudent risk management form the foundation of our

value. We uphold our commitment to compliance, engage stakeholders through open and proactive dialogue, and build lasting trust over time. We regard talent as the cornerstone of enterprise development and support their development at every stage. Besides, customer satisfaction drives us to continuously enhance service quality, while we work with suppliers to build a value ecosystem grounded in integrity, transparency, and green collaboration. We also take active part in environmental education, community service, and rural revitalisation, contributing to the improvement of urban and rural environments and the enhancement of public services, ensuring that the fruits of high-quality development are shared across society.

Clean water safeguards the ecosystem, and green water secures a sustainable future. At BEWG, we embrace climate action and environmental protection as core responsibilities. We have established a three-tier climate governance structure, spanning from the Board to the execution level, fully integrating climate-related risks and opportunities into strategic planning and risk management. We have set clear carbon reduction targets, i.e., advancing energy efficiency and conservation with our proprietary low-carbon technologies such as BEAOA and BESWIFT, while optimising our energy mix and lowering our operational carbon footprint through the deployment of photovoltaic power and energy-recovery technologies, including water source heat pumps. In ecological protection, we strictly follow the strategy of "avoid-reduce-restore-regenerate-transform", incorporating biodiversity impact assessments and ecological restoration throughout the project lifecycle. Through concrete actions, we ensure the harmonious coexistence of human activities and the natural world.

As we step into this new era, BEWG will embrace change with even stronger strategic determination. Looking ahead to 2026, we will continue to follow the "W.I.S.E." action direction, staying focused on our core mission, deepening digital-intelligent integration and low-carbon transition, and continuously improving operational effectiveness and governance. We firmly believe that the value of water services lies in safeguarding life supporting ecosystems, and empowering the future. Moving forward, BEWG will work alongside partners across sectors, leveraging our strengths through collaboration and determined actions, to jointly write a new chapter of sustainable development for this era of lucid waters and lush mountains.

ESG Governance

Sustainability Governance Structure

BEWG attaches great importance to corporate ESG governance and has always complied with the Corporate Governance Code set out in Appendix C1 to the Listing Rules of The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Limited and the relevant domestic and overseas regulatory requirements in the places of operation. The Group continuously improves ESG governance to safeguard shareholders' rights and better serve the interests of stakeholders.

BEWG has established a comprehensive and efficient ESG governance framework and built a long-term ESG working mechanism to further implement sustainability management and continuously enhance the Group's sustainability competitiveness.

The Board, as the highest decision-making body, is responsible for identifying and determining material ESG issues, and advises on the Group's ESG targets, policies and structure. Besides, it also guides the Group's overall strategy and oversees management.

The Sustainability Committee oversees the implementation of specific ESG matters and reports to the Board on the progress and achievements of ESG management. It also takes the responsibility for identifying material ESG issues, assessing climate-related risks and opportunities, reviewing environmental target achievement, and evaluating the impact of the Group's ESG performance on stakeholders.

To ensure effective ESG management practices, we have established an ESG Working Group comprising various business units and functional departments. This working group coordinates and drives the implementation of specific ESG projects, and regularly reports to management and the Board to ensure smooth ESG progress and effective risk prevention.

Additionally, climate change management and oversight functions have been integrated into the Board, the Sustainability Committee, and the ESG Working Group to continuously improve the effectiveness of climate governance and management.

  • • Establish, guide, oversee, and review the vision, goals, policies, implementation, and management guidelines for sustainability;
  • • Identify and prioritise material ESG issues;
  • • Oversee the communication process with the stakeholders;
  • • Identify potential risks and opportunities related to sustainability issues and assess their impacts;
  • • Review and ensure the establishment of appropriate and effective sustainability risk management and internal control systems;
  • • Review work related to climate change, including the management and oversight of climate change issues;

Pipeline network construction

Emergency Response

In response to possible sudden influent shock and irregular influent fluctuations faced by sewage treatment plants, we have established an emergency management mechanism and a long-term management mechanism. While strengthening our internal emergency response capabilities, we actively collaborate with government agencies and upstream businesses to establish a coordinated support network, thereby systematically enhancing the operational resilience and risk-resistance capabilities of sewage treatment plants.

Emergency Management for Influent Shock

When faced with sudden high pollutant concentration influent, abnormal influent pollutants, or sudden increases in influent volume, we take a series of emergency management measures inside and outside the sewage treatment plant to quickly restore stable operation of the plant and ensure stable compliance of effluent water quality.

On-Site Emergency Response

Activate the emergency plan and conduct continuous monitoring and analysis of the influent quality. Organise technical experts to analyse the influent situation and the treatment capacity of the current treatment processes and facilities for the influent. Adjust technical parameters and chemical dosing amounts of each process based on the influent water temperature conditions, pollutant components and concentrations.

Off-Site Emergency Coordination

Arrange dedicated personnel to inspect the upstream external pipeline network to identify the source of the influent shock, report abnormalities to the superior competent department at the first time with a written report document, while entrusting a third party to conduct sampling and testing to trace the cause of the influent shock.

Long-Term Management for Influent Shock

For projects where industrial wastewater accounts for a significant proportion of the influent, wastewater from industrial parks often contains industrial wastewater of varying nature such as chemicals, pharmaceuticals, and metal smelting. Since the quality and volume of such wastewater fluctuate frequently and without any obvious pattern, sewage treatment plant may face a significant risk of influent shock. To this end, through strengthened upstream control and internal emergency drills, we have established a long-term management mechanism for prevention and emergency response to address the challenges posed by influent shocks, achieving process stability, effluent compliance, and cost control.

Upstream Point Source Control

Strengthened Management Foundations: Formulate the Pipeline Network Inspection Management Policy and utilise professional tools to improve the efficiency of pipeline network inspections; Establish drainage archives, draw pipeline network maps, and summarise enterprise discharge points, drainage paths, key checkpoints, and drainage characteristics to guide inspection work. Based on this, regular analysis reports on sewage pipeline network are conducted to systematically identify the sources of illegal inflow, seasonal flow fluctuations, and water quality anomalies, thereby enhancing the ability to detect abnormal conditions and reduce operational risks.

Government Collaboration and Support: Pipeline network inspectors go to upstream enterprises to take samples for analysis while coordinating with law enforcement departments to increase supervision efforts. The government organises enterprises to install automatic valves at legal drainage points, which automatically close when emissions exceed standards.

Collaboration with Upstream Enterprises: Sign drainage agreements with key upstream drainage enterprises, to systematically understand their production characteristics, wastewater discharge patterns, pollutant information, so as to precisely respond to their service demands; Provide professional training to personnel and help upstream enterprises optimise wastewater pretreatment processes to reduce pollutant discharge concentrations.

Internal Emergency Drills

Develop and improve localised Emergency Plan to Abnormal Influent for different abnormal influent situations based on project conditions; Enhance multi-departmental coordination and employees' professional emergency response capabilities through multiple simulated drills, to ensure efficient collaboration and rapid response among pipeline network, quality control, and operation and maintenance departments during emergencies.

"Regenerate" Action: Qingquan River Constructed Wetland Project

The Qingquan River constructed wetland project in Liaocheng, Shandong adopts a combined process of horizontal subsurface flow and surface flow wetlands, and is primarily used for advanced treatment of effluent from the Guan County wastewater treatment plant, with treated water discharged into the Qingquan River. The wetland is designed to treat 80,000 tonnes of reclaimed water per day. The effluent meets the Class IV standards under the Environmental Quality Standards for Surface Water (GB 3838-2002), and exceeds Class III standards for more than 80% of the days. Annually, it reduces COD by 84 tonnes and ammonia nitrogen by 14.6 tonnes.

The construction and operation of the wetland have not only significantly improved the water quality of the Qingquan River, but have also created a dynamic wetland ecological landscape for Guan County. The wetland has become an essential near-natural waterfront recreational space for local residents. The project covers an area of 150,000 square metres, including 50,000 square metres of open water and 100,000 square metres of planted aquatic vegetation, trees and shrubs. Wetland plants such as cattails, sweet flags, pickerelweed, bulrush, yellow flag iris, canna, purple loosestrife and lotus flourish, directly expanding the range of available habitats for biodiversity. Since its completion, more than 30 bird species have been recorded, representing an increase of 80% compared with pre-construction levels. In winter, the maximum observed number of waterfowl (such as geese and ducks) exceeded 100 individuals in a single observation. Fish species have recovered from nearly zero to eight species, and three species of amphibians and reptiles have been identified.

Biodiversity Protection at Daoxianghu Underground Reclaimed Water Plant

The Daoxianghu Water Plant in Beijing is located adjacent to Cuihu National Urban Wetland Park. Situated in the northern Haidian area, it forms an important node of the "Western Hills-Yongding River" ecological corridor and serves as the "Northern Ecological and Technological Green Core" of Haidian, playing a key role in guiding high-quality development of urban and ecological spaces. The plant's ecological water replenishment and landscape greening projects, together with Cuihu Wetland Park and Wenquan Park, form an integrated ecological network combining "points, lines and surfaces".

The plant adopts a model of "fully underground treatment + surface park", with a 20,000 m2 ecological park constructed above ground and a green coverage rate exceeding 80%, significantly improving vegetation coverage compared with traditional water plants. The total site area is only 4.66 hectares, achieving more than 70% land-saving compared with conventional above-ground plants of similar scale, reducing the occupation of surrounding farmland and green spaces and preserving ecological buffer areas. In addition, through underground enclosed treatment, multi-stage biological deodorisation and noise control technologies, the plant has effectively resolved issues of odour nuisance and noise pollution associated with traditional facilities. A 200 m2 water technology exhibition hall has been established, and public outreach activities such as "Ecological Open Days" are conducted, receiving over 800 visitors annually and effectively promoting concepts of water recycling and ecological protection, achieving both recreational and educational value.

The plant uses high-quality reclaimed water as a core source for ecological replenishment, establishing a complete water cycle system of "wastewater collection – purification treatment – reuse – ecological restoration" for the Nansha River basin. In 2025, more than 40 million tonnes of reclaimed water were supplied to the Nansha River. Following replenishment, water quality improved from below Class V to stable Class IV54, resolving issues of seasonal flow interruption and black and odorous water, enhancing water circulation and exchange, and strengthening the self-purification capacity of the river. After restoration, the Nansha River has become a "green corridor" connecting ecological patches, facilitating genetic exchange and species migration, and enhancing ecosystem connectivity and integrity across the region.
